Definition: to widen (in any direction), i.e. (intransitively) recede or (transitively) remove (literally or figuratively, of place or relation)
BiblicalUsage: Rachaq is to widen, to recede, to remove far off — of place or of relation. Agur prayed, 'Remove far from me vanity and lies'; the psalm says, 'As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us'; and Isaiah confesses, 'Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.'
TheologicalSignificance: This tells me that the distance runs both ways: God removes our sins far from us, and our sins remove His judgment far from us — and the prayer is that He would close the second distance and keep the first.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
